replies.text: Think of pricing not as a formula… but as a geometry of market states: • Flat region → Black-Scholes works • Curved region → smile appears So the “failure” of BSM is structured.
Most models try to fit the volatility smile. The approach considered here explains why it exists. It’s curvature. And that curvature has a specific structure.

In this framework: • BSM = flat slice • Smile = curvature • SABR β = 1 emerges structurally Empirically: Skew predicted from SPY/VIX time series → matches LEAPS within ~20% - with no options calibration step.

The deeper result: Market time dynamics and the volatility surface are two projections of the same underlying geometry. Same structure → • momentum dynamics • volatility smile Still exploring the connection.

You could try restating it as a stress tensor with the linear vectors combining at certain points to produce exponential or discontinuous jumps. You are 100% correct about the issues once things depart from normalcy, where the big risks emerge.

Right that departures from normality are where the risks live. Small clarification: paper uses a metric tensor (Fisher information), not a stress tensor. Different objects, related role: geometry and curvature. Smile = leading-order curvature. Jumps live one level above, §7.6.
